title: NABH Hospital Accreditation
shortDescription: The ten chapters every NABH-accredited hospital is assessed against — current (6th Edition) naming, with the one major rename exams love to test.
genZNote: Ten chapters. One of them changed its name recently. That's exactly the kind of thing an exam asks.

sections.heading: Current Edition — Read This First
sections.body: NABH's Hospital Accreditation Standards are periodically revised. The 5th Edition (2020) is now the HISTORICAL/previous edition. The 6th Edition became effective from 1 January 2025 and is CURRENT for new accreditation applications. The most exam-relevant change: the infection-control chapter was renamed from 'Hospital Infection Control (HIC)' in the 5th Edition to 'Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)' in the 6th Edition — same domain, updated name and scope. Both editions keep the same overall count of ten chapters.

sections.heading: The Ten Standard Areas (Current — 6th Edition Naming)
sections.body: Each area covers a distinct domain of hospital functioning, assessed through detailed objective elements underneath it.
bullets: Access, Assessment and Continuity of Care (AAC) — the patient's entire journey from arrival/registration through assessment, care planning, and discharge or transfer. Exam fact: this is typically one of the largest, most objective-element-dense chapters. Common confusion: students conflate this with 'Care of Patients' — AAC is about the JOURNEY and process flow, COP is about the clinical care content itself.

Care of Patients (COP) — clinical care processes and protocols: how patients are actually treated, from routine care to high-risk procedures. Why it matters: this is where clinical protocol adherence is directly assessed.

Management of Medication (MOM) — the full medication lifecycle: prescribing, storage, dispensing, administration, and monitoring for errors. Exam fact: medication error prevention (e.g. look-alike/sound-alike drug controls) sits squarely here.

Patient Rights and Education (PRE) — informed consent, patient rights, grievance mechanisms, and patient/family education about their own care. Common confusion: PRE is about RIGHTS and EDUCATION, not clinical content — that's COP's job.

Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) — renamed from 'Hospital Infection Control (HIC)' in the 6th Edition; covers surveillance, hand hygiene, sterilisation, and (per the 6th Edition update) dedicated antimicrobial stewardship requirements. Exam fact: know BOTH names — IPC is current, HIC is what older material/5th-Edition questions may still call it.
Patient Safety and Quality Improvement (PSQ) — the hospital's systematic patient-safety programme: incident reporting, quality indicators, sentinel event review, and improvement cycles.
Responsibilities of Management (ROM) — governance, leadership accountability, and organisational planning for quality and safety.
Facilities Management and Safety (FMS) — the physical environment: fire safety, utilities, equipment safety, and emergency preparedness for the building/infrastructure itself.
Human Resource Management (HRM) — credentialing, training, competency assessment, and staff records — proving the PEOPLE are qualified, not just the processes.
Information Management System (IMS) — medical record-keeping, data security, and (a 6th Edition emphasis) digital health/EMR integration.

sections.heading: A Note on Common Confusion Across Chapters
sections.body: Students frequently mix up AAC (process/journey) with COP (clinical content), and PRE (rights/education) with COP (clinical care) — the safest way to keep them straight is to ask: is this about the PATH the patient takes, the RIGHTS/INFORMATION they receive, or the actual CLINICAL CARE given? That question maps cleanly onto AAC, PRE, and COP respectively.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: NABH's Hospital Accreditation Standards are organised into ten chapters covering the full scope of hospital functioning — currently the 6th Edition (effective 1 January 2025), which renamed the infection-control chapter from HIC to IPC.
keyFacts: Current: NABH Hospital Accreditation Standards, 6th Edition, effective 1 January 2025.
Historical: 5th Edition (2020) — do not present as current.
The infection-control chapter is now IPC (Infection Prevention and Control); it was HIC (Hospital Infection Control) in the 5th Edition.
Ten chapters, both editions: AAC, COP, MOM, PRE, IPC/HIC, PSQ, ROM, FMS, HRM, IMS.
commonConfusion: AAC vs. COP — AAC is the patient's journey/process flow; COP is the actual clinical care content.
IPC vs. HIC — same chapter, IPC is the current (6th Edition) name, HIC is the historical (5th Edition) name.

highYieldFacts: 6th Edition is current (from 1 Jan 2025); 5th Edition (2020) is historical.
IPC replaced HIC as the infection-control chapter's name in the 6th Edition.
Both editions retain ten chapters covering the same overall domains.
commonTraps: Writing 'HIC' as if it's the current chapter name — check which edition a question is set in.
mustRemember: AAC → COP → MOM → PRE → IPC → PSQ → ROM → FMS → HRM → IMS — ten chapters, current 6th Edition names.

confusedTerms.termA: AAC (Access, Assessment and Continuity of Care)
confusedTerms.distinction: AAC is about the patient's journey and process flow through the hospital; COP is about the actual clinical care and treatment protocols given.
Same chapter, different edition names — Infection Prevention and Control (6th Edition, current) was called Hospital Infection Control (5th Edition, historical).

possibleQuestions: List the ten NABH hospital standard chapters using current (6th Edition) naming.

questions.prompt: What is the CURRENT name of the NABH chapter that covers infection surveillance, hand hygiene, and antimicrobial stewardship?
questions.explanation: IPC is the 6th Edition (current) name; HIC was the 5th Edition (historical) name for the same domain.

questions.prompt: Which chapter covers the patient's journey from arrival/registration through assessment, care planning, and discharge?
options: Access, Assessment and Continuity of Care (AAC)
questions.explanation: AAC covers the process/journey; COP covers the actual clinical care content given along that journey.

questions.prompt: The NABH Hospital Accreditation Standards, 6th Edition, became effective from:
options: It has no fixed effective date
questions.explanation: The 6th Edition became effective for new accreditation applications from 1 January 2025.
